dish: Fluffy griddle hotcakes (plain, blueberry, banana or chocolate-chip) and homestyle breakfast
w: Downtown Altoona's counter-and-booths diner since 1933, run by three generations of the Batrus/George family. Its griddle hotcakes are a local institution; a longtime stop on any Altoona diner crawl.

dish: Texas hot dog — steamed dog topped with the George family's all-beef Greek-style chili sauce; also chili over macaroni
w: Founded 1918 by Greek immigrant Peter George, who built his Texas-style all-beef chili sauce after a chance meeting with a Greek man from Texas. Still run by his descendants with the secret recipe intact — an Altoona coney institution that passed its 100th year in 2018.

dish: Altoona-style pizza — Sicilian square crust, tomato sauce, sliced green pepper and salami under a lid of yellow American cheese
w: The keeper of Altoona-style ('Altoona Hotel') pizza, the internet-famous square slice invented at the long-gone Altoona Hotel: green bell pepper and salami beneath melted American cheese on Sicilian dough. Owner Steve Corklic's shop is the slice's best-known standard-bearer since the hotel burned in 2013.

dish: Mallo Cup — coconut-flecked milk-chocolate cup with a whipped marshmallow center (America's first cup candy, 1936)
w: Depression-era Altoona candy maker founded by brothers Bill and Bob Boyer, who invented the Mallo Cup in 1936 — the first cup candy in America, still made downtown along with Smoothie peanut-butter cups. Factory outlet store on-site with the collectible 'Mallo Cup points.'

dish: American tavern fare and rotating craft brews in an 1835 canal-era hotel barroom
w: Historic Hollidaysburg hotel dating to 1835 on the Pennsylvania Canal / Allegheny Portage route, rebuilt in 1886 by a Bavarian brewmaster with a cut-block barroom added in 1905. Now a restored tavern for American plates, craft beer and cocktails inside the NRHP-listed Hollidaysburg Historic District.

dish: Fresh-churned frozen custard (the original 1950 Meadows recipe)
address: 1710 E Pleasant Valley Blvd, Altoona, PA 16602
w: The frozen-custard brand born in Altoona on July 4, 1950, when the Meadows brothers perfected the recipe still used today. Now a multi-location Pennsylvania institution; the Altoona-area stands are the original home turf.

Huntingdon's community coffeehouse and specialty roaster, open since 2008 in a former laundromat; roasts ~22,000 lbs a year for 40+ wholesale clients across Central PA. Espresso bar, paninis, soups and a sun-drenched patio near Raystown Lake and Juniata College.
